course_name_original: Ingeniería de fabricación y calidad dimensional
prerequisites: Fundamentals of manufacturing systems and technologies
Ability to use dimensional measurement and verification instruments in the lab/workshop.
Ability to use statistics in Quality Control.
Ability to dimension and define tolerances adequately and precisely for mechanical elements.
Ability to represent basic parts and assemblies using 3D CAD.
Ability to use and know manual machine tools and their basic operations.
Ability to develop basic NC programs for lathe and milling machine, and select tools.
Ability to plan machining, deformation, and welding processes to produce basic parts and/or assemblies.
Ability to apply Elasticity theory and know how to represent stress states through Mohr's circles.

learning_outcomes.text: Know the technological basis and basic aspects of manufacturing processes.
Understand the basic aspects of manufacturing systems.
Acquire skills for selecting manufacturing processes and developing manufacturing planning.
Develop skills for manufacturing assemblies and elements in CADCAM environments.

syllabus_topics: Modeling and simulation of mechanical manufacturing processes
Analysis, implementation, and optimization of forming processes
Lines and Systems of Mechanical Manufacturing and their simulation: CAM Systems. 'Transfer' systems. Production lines. Flexible manufacturing systems and cells. Integrated manufacturing.

Planning of manufacturing processes: Analysis of the design drawing. Selection of processes and determination of the manufacturing sequence. Definition of process sheet. Technological management of manufacturing.
The scope of dimensional metrology. Precision in industry. Measurement errors. Measurement chains.
Systems, machines, inspection, and verification equipment in Mechanical Manufacturing.
Modeling and measurement of surface quality.
Calibration. Metrological organization. Measurement uncertainty. Traceability and dissemination. Calibration plan.
Statistical process control. Control charts by variables. Control charts by attributes. Machine and process capability.
Quality of measurements in industry. Evaluation of measurement quality. Tools and techniques for evaluating dimensional quality and its costs.
Metrological techniques and systems. Legal and industrial metrology.

assessment_methods.method: Practice reports, practicum, and external internships

assessment_rules: Ethical commitment is expected; unethical behavior (copying, plagiarism, unauthorized electronic devices) will result in a 0.0 final grade for the academic year. For the first attempt, students can choose between two evaluation systems: A. Without Continuous Evaluation, which is based on a final exam (20% multiple-choice test, 80% problems/exercises). B. Continuous Evaluation, consisting of two partial exams (40% each) and justification of practices/exercises (20%). To pass, a minimum of 40% must be obtained in each evaluable part; otherwise, the maximum global grade will be 4.9. For the second and subsequent attempts, only System A (final exam) will be used, and no parts or contents evaluated in the same or previous courses will be recognized.
